item.title: UMich, PSI researchers report new airborne radiation-detection method
item.dc:creator: Nuclear News Staff
item.description:
Researchers from the University of Michigan College of Engineering and Switzerland’s Paul Scherrer Institute are reporting the development of a new airborne method of radiation detection that accurately identifies single or mixed source identity, activity, and location. Their research has been published in Nature Communications under the title “Quantitative Mobile Gamma-Ray Spectrometry through Bayesian Inference.”

The research is expected to improve the work of emergency responders by enabling them to more quickly and precisely determine where people in radiologically hazardous situations—such as a nuclear reactor meltdown or a nuclear weapon detonation—should evacuate for safe shelter. The research also should help responders better determine what other types of protective measures should be implemented for such people, including distribution of protective equipment and potassium iodide pills (which protect the thyroid gland from radiation).

item.title: Nucleon Fuel seeks $20M grant for Wyo. conversion facility
item.dc:creator: Nuclear News Staff
item.description:
Nucleon Fuel, a subsidiary of Canadian small modular reactor developer Nucleon Energy, has applied for a $20 million grant and possible $10 million additional loan to build a uranium conversion facility near Gillette, Wyo.

Both the grant and the loan would be funded by Wyoming’s recently created Energy Dominance Fund, which seeks to advance projects related to oil, natural gas, coal, and nuclear energy in the state.
